intervention_label: Confirmatory diagnostic gate: high-resolution HLA class I typing (A*02:01, A*24:02) + HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of patient AND sibling donor + comprehensive relapse NGS resolving TP53/Y220C + STR chimerism on sorted CD34+ blasts
expected_benefit: Resolves the three pending gates that decide the whole plan. HLA-A*02:01 typing plus a recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1(H)-negative mismatch open HA-directed TCR-T (rank 6); A*02:01 alone (or A*24:02) opens the WT1 axis (rank 10); variant-level NGS confirming TP53-aberrant then Y220C opens rezatapopt (rank 11). STR chimerism on FACS-sorted CD34+ blasts confirms recipient-origin relapse, a prerequisite for any minor-antigen TCR-T and for the second-transplant strategy.
key_risks: Records retrieval same-day; repeat HLA typing 3-7 days; HA-1/HA-2 genotyping 1-2 weeks (often via the trial central lab); NGS 1-3 weeks; sorted-CD34 STR chimerism 1-2 weeks
HA-1/HA-2 standalone genotyping is not a routine catalog test and usually runs through the therapy sponsor or an academic immunogenetics lab
the TP53 discrepancy must not be collapsed in either direction; read the NGS with p53 IHC, 17p FISH, and the retrieved 2019 variant identity together
preference_alignment: Aligns with every stated preference: non-toxic, runs on archived records plus blood/marrow and a paired sibling-donor sample, and it is the single action that moves the HLA-restricted axis the patient came here for from undetermined to eligible. Matches prefers_trials (gates enrollment); no toxicity veto tripped.
guideline_status: Implicit prerequisite of every downstream trial and label; NCT05473910 (HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T) requires HLA-A*02:01 + the mHAg mismatch, NCT06616636 (rezatapopt) requires confirmed TP53 Y220C.
rationale_summary: All five personas placed their entire ranking downstream of this workup, so it is the one unanimous first action. The case was submitted for the HLA-restricted immunotherapy axis, and eligibility is doubly unresolved: HLA-A*02:01 is only a chart placeholder and HA-1/HA-2 has not been genotyped in either the patient or the sibling donor. The TP53 handle is separately double-gated, since the 2019-pathogenic-versus-2026-negative discrepancy sits on a 2%-LOD, CNV-blind panel and the specific variant is unknown. STR chimerism on sorted CD34+ blasts is load-bearing because a donor-derived leukemia would redirect the whole plan and because HA-directed TCR-T targets recipient-restricted antigens. None of it is toxic, and each result independently opens or forecloses a downstream option.
open_questions: Whether the 2020 allele-level HLA typing can be retrieved from the first-transplant / donor-registry chart or must be repeated
Whether standalone HA-1/HA-2 genotyping is run through the ALLOHA sponsor central lab or an academic immunogenetics lab
Whether the retrieved 2019 TP53 variant is Y220C specifically, and whether 17p FISH / p53 IHC support a copy-loss or multi-hit aberration
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic certainty - independently resolves HLA-A*02:01, the HA-1/HA-2 mismatch, TP53/Y220C status, and recipient-clonal origin; each gate opens or forecloses one downstream option.
toxicity_burden: Low (none - records retrieval plus assays on blood, marrow, and a paired sibling-donor sample)
overall: The non-toxic gate the whole plan waits on; retrieving HLA typing and genotyping the sibling pair is what turns the stated-reason immunotherapy axis from undetermined into eligible.

intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2) for relapse after first allo-HCT
expected_benefit: The only modality here with a real cure fraction: ~37% 2-year OS in the matched-related-donor subgroup of the Christopeit EBMT registry, versus ~25% pooled. Her ~6-year first remission sits on the favorable side of that curve.
key_risks: Substantial non-relapse mortality and GVHD in a second allograft, not broken out in the abstract-level registry
undeliverable at 85% marrow blasts without effective cytoreduction to a transplantable state first
conditioning intensity cannot be chosen safely without the missing cardiac / organ-function workup
preference_alignment: Fully matches curative intent and the explicitly-acceptable-modality set (HCT2 named as an acceptable handle, no modality vetoed). The 0.75 efficacy lean supports it; the file's own open fitness flag qualifies the conditioning choice.
guideline_status: NCCN AML v4.2026 category 2A for post-transplant relapse in fit patients; ELN 2022 places HCT2 at the center of curative-intent management once the marrow is back in remission.
rationale_summary: Conservative and concensusite ranked this first and everyone else built around it; the critic and advocate endorsed it in round 2, so agreement is unanimous. It is the platform every downstream cellular play, HA-1 TCR-T and DLI included, has to ride on. The honest limits are that the headline 37% is a fitness-selected related-donor subgroup of a retrospective registry (ROBINS-I Serious), and active high-burden disease at transplant is the dominant adverse survival driver in the same analysis, which is exactly where she sits at 85% blasts. The disease also escaped graft-versus-leukemia once already, so a durable HCT2 is not assured even with a good first remission. The rank rests on cytoreduction working first and on a fitness assessment that has not been done.
open_questions: Same HLA-identical sibling versus an alternative donor, informed by the HA-1/HA-2 genotyping already underway
Cardiac / organ-function fitness and goals-of-care assessment, currently undocumented
Whether cytoreduction can bring the 85%-blast marrow close enough to remission to make HCT2 deliverable
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate in this subset - ~37% 2-year OS in matched-related-donor HCT2 (Christopeit 2013), lifted by her ~6-year first remission but pulled down by 85% blasts.
toxicity_burden: High (non-relapse mortality and acute/chronic GVHD substantial in a second allograft; infection; conditioning organ toxicity)

counter_productive_moa.description: Disease already escaped graft-versus-leukemia once; TP53-aberrant complex-karyotype biology predicts renewed immune escape after HCT2

overall: The curative backbone with a real cure fraction, but only deliverable after cytoreduction and a fitness workup that has not been done; disease burden at transplant dominates the odds.

intervention_label: Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab, anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning) into HCT2
expected_benefit: SIERRA (randomized phase 3) reported durable CR (>=180 days) 17.1% vs 0% (p<0.0001) and EFS HR 0.23 - the strongest evidence in the dossier that CD45-targeted conditioning can carry an active, high-blast marrow into an allograft. Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs were 59.7% vs 59.2% on conventional care, so the targeted conditioning did not add toxicity on top of what these patients already face.
key_risks: Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs ~60% (cytopenias, febrile neutropenia, infection, mucositis) - as expected for myeloablative conditioning
ITT OS was flat (HR 0.99, p=0.96), read as a crossover artifact (52% of controls crossed over) rather than proven survival benefit
marrow-directed conditioning may not clear the extramedullary thigh sarcoma, which needs separate directed-RT planning
preference_alignment: Matches curative intent, no modality veto, prefers_trials including travel (the go-forward study is trial-only). The 0.75 efficacy lean argues for the enabler; the open fitness axis should set conditioning intensity.
guideline_status: Investigational; CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning is not yet adopted by NCCN or ELN. SIERRA (NCT02665065) is closed; the go-forward study is NCT07157514.
rationale_summary: Every persona endorsed this on the evidence, even concensusite, who ranked it last only because NCCN/ELN have not adopted CD45 RIT - a guideline-lag objection that the risktaker and advocate explicitly pushed back on. The critic conceded it is the one tier-1b anchor in the file. The load-bearing caveat is eligibility, not toxicity: SIERRA enrolled patients heading to a FIRST transplant, so prior-allo-HCT candidacy has to be verified against the NCT07157514 protocol, which is not yet recruiting. It competes with FLAMSA-RIC (rank 7) for the same conditioning job. Conservative endorsed the AE-parity signal but held the go/no-go contingent on a fitness assessment.
open_questions: Whether the go-forward apamistamab protocol (NCT07157514) accepts a prior allo-HCT
When NCT07157514 opens to enrollment
Whether the extramedullary thigh sarcoma needs directed radiotherapy alongside marrow-directed conditioning
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate - durable CR 17.1% vs 0% (SIERRA phase 3, EFS HR 0.23); ITT OS flat (HR 0.99) with 52% crossover; prior-HCT eligibility unverified.
toxicity_burden: High (grade >=3 treatment-related AEs ~60%: cytopenias, febrile neutropenia, infection, mucositis)

counter_productive_moa.description: Marrow-directed CD45 conditioning may spare the extramedullary thigh sarcoma sanctuary site, leaving a source of relapse; needs directed RT

overall: The RCT-grade enabler that could carry an 85%-blast marrow into HCT2, gated on verifying prior-transplant eligibility against the not-yet-open go-forward protocol.

intervention_label: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin (Mylotarg, CD33 ADC) as cytoreductive bridge
expected_benefit: The one on-label, immediately prescribable agent on the slate for her confirmed CD33-positive blasts. Sievers reported ~30% overall remission (CR+CRp) in CD33+ AML in first relapse - a CD33-directed debulk toward HCT2, not a definitive answer.
key_risks: Grade >=3 hyperbilirubinemia 23% and transaminase elevation 17%; veno-occlusive disease is the characteristic class risk and stacks peri-transplant
single-agent depth ~30% comes from a less-pretreated first-relapse population than this patient
benefit tracks CD33 antigen density, and only qualitative positivity is on file
preference_alignment: Matches curative-intent bridging and the no-modality-veto set; it is the CD33 handle that is available by routine prescription rather than a trial. Density-guided go/no-go respects the efficacy lean.
guideline_status: FDA-approved on-label for CD33-positive relapsed AML; NCCN AML v4.2026 carries single-agent gemtuzumab at category 2A.
rationale_summary: Conservative, critic, and concensusite all ranked this as the on-label CD33-directed cytoreductive bridge, and concensusite defended it against the critic's evidence-quality downgrade on the grounds that a 2A rating is the panel's own calibration of exactly that single-arm data plus twenty-plus years of VOD-monitoring experience. The honest ceiling is modest and drawn from a population less heavily pretreated than she is, with prior MDS, FLAG-IDA/venetoclax failure, and a myeloid sarcoma. The calicheamicin hepatotoxicity/VOD signal is the reason to leave an adequate interval and consider fractionated dosing before HCT2. Quantitative CD33 antigen density is the pending readout that should anchor the go/no-go, since qualitative positivity is not ADC-predictive density.
open_questions: Quantitative CD33 antigen density (antibodies-bound-per-cell), still pending
Adequate interval and fractionation relative to a planned HCT2 to limit VOD
Whether it debulks the extramedullary thigh sarcoma at all
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-moderate - ~30% CR+CRp in less-pretreated first relapse (Sievers 2001); likely lower post-FLAG-IDA/venetoclax; density-dependent, quantitative CD33 pending.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (grade >=3 hyperbilirubinemia 23%, transaminitis 17%, infection 28%; veno-occlusive disease class risk peri-transplant)

counter_productive_moa.description: Calicheamicin hepatotoxicity / VOD could compromise the very HCT2 it is meant to bridge to; time the interval accordingly

overall: The only agent a treating team can simply write; a modest on-label CD33 debulk whose VOD signal has to be timed around the planned second transplant.

intervention_label: Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) from the sibling donor
expected_benefit: The one comparative signal in the transplant set: 21% vs 9% 2-year OS with versus without DLI (adjusted P=0.04), and her ~6-year late relapse is exactly the feature that predicts DLI benefit. Best used as an adjunct to the transplant platform, not standalone.
key_risks: Given into active high-burden disease the same series shows ~15% 2-year OS - she is in that worse stratum at 85% blasts
GVHD is the characteristic toxicity and would complicate a subsequent HCT2
the registry benefit is a selection-confounded minority effect
preference_alignment: Matches curative intent and the no-modality-veto set; the sibling donor makes it readily available. Best sequenced after cytoreduction, consistent with the efficacy lean.
guideline_status: ASTCT/EBMT-recognized for AML relapse after allo-HCT; ELN 2022 frames immunosuppression taper plus cytoreduction plus adoptive cells as the combination that occasionally yields durable remissions.
rationale_summary: The critic and concensusite ranked DLI as an adjunct on the strength of the Schmid registry, and both were explicit that the number is confounding-by-indication wearing a p-value. Benefit concentrated in the remission / favorable-karyotype group (~56%); the active-disease or aplasia stratum she falls in came in around 15%. Every persona who touched it read it the same way: an argument for cytoreduction before any DLI, not for DLI into a florid marrow. It pairs naturally with the FLAMSA-RIC prophylactic-DLI schedule and with the sibling-donor HCT2 plan rather than competing with them.
open_questions: Whether the sibling donor is available and willing to donate lymphocytes again
How to sequence DLI relative to cytoreduction and HCT2 to avoid infusing into high-burden disease
GVHD risk if combined with HLA-restricted TCR-T consolidation
likelihood_of_effect: Low for this stratum - 21% vs 9% 2-year OS overall (Schmid 2007), but ~15% in the active-disease group she falls in at 85% blasts.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (acute/chronic GVHD is the characteristic toxicity; marrow aplasia when given into active disease)

counter_productive_moa.description: DLI into 85% blasts drives GVHD without meaningful graft-versus-leukemia; demands cytoreduction to remission first

overall: A readily available sibling-donor adjunct whose honest expectation is modest in florid disease; belongs after cytoreduction, alongside the transplant, not as standalone salvage.

intervention_label: HA-1 / HA-2-directed donor TCR-T after HCT2 (Bleakley platform; TSC-100 / TSC-101, ALLOHA; BSB-1001)
expected_benefit: The stated reason for the run and the highest-ceiling cure swing: donor TCR-T aims graft-versus-leukemia at recipient blood-lineage cells while mostly sparing the tissues that drive GVHD. Bleakley's phase 1 got 4 of 9 recurrent post-HCT patients into or holding CR, with one remission past two years and no dose-limiting toxicity; TSC-100/101 and BSB-1001 are recruiting on the back of a fresh matched transplant.
key_risks: Feasibility signal only (n=9); the per-term grade-level AE table could not be retrieved from the Blood 2024 full text, so 'no DLTs' is the only safety datum on file
characteristic setting risks are lymphodepletion cytopenias and GVHD
delivered on the back of HCT2 (rank 2), so it does nothing for the current 85%-blast marrow
preference_alignment: The single most preference-aligned option: curative intent, prefers_trials including travel, no toxicity veto tripped. The tension is eligibility, not preference - two personas dissented on evidence maturity and fitness, so it is carried with caveats.
guideline_status: Investigational, no consensus category of its own; NCCN AML v4.2026 and ELN 2022 both make trial enrollment the preferred R/R route, which makes this a guideline-consistent enrollment target rather than a guideline-endorsed modality.
rationale_summary: Conditional on HLA-A*02:01-positive AND a recipient HA-1(H)/HA-2-positive, donor-negative mismatch. Foreclosed if either is negative. In the positive branch the eligibility gate that drove conservative to park it and the critic to rank it last is resolved, but their objections do not fully lift: the evidence-maturity dissent (n=9 single-arm feasibility, unretrievable AE table) and the fitness caution persist independent of the biomarker, so both stay in dissent. The risktaker, advocate, and concensusite endorse it as the axis the case was submitted for, with concensusite framing it through the guideline's enroll-in-a-trial language. This is the preference-conflict case the rules flag: advocate ranked it first as preference-aligned while >=2 personas dissented, so status is considered_with_caveats and the tension is surfaced rather than flattened. The load-bearing gate is the HA-1/HA-2 mismatch - a biological coin-flip that genotyping the pair simply closes.
open_questions: Whether the recipient HA-1(H)/HA-2-positive, donor-negative mismatch actually exists once the pair is genotyped
Which enrolling program (TScan ALLOHA, Fred Hutch, BlueSphere BSB-1001) can hold a screening slot
Whether recipient-origin relapse is confirmed by sorted-CD34 STR chimerism, a prerequisite for mHAg targeting
scenario_label: If HLA-A*02:01-positive AND a recipient HA-1(H)/HA-2-positive, donor-negative mismatch is confirmed in the patient and sibling
likelihood_of_effect: Signal-level, positive branch - 4/9 CR with one remission >2 years and no DLTs (Bleakley n=9); feasibility, not efficacy-powered. Foreclosed if typing is negative.
toxicity_burden: Low (no DLTs across n=9; lymphodepletion cytopenias and GVHD are the setting risks; per-grade AE table not retrievable from the full text)

counter_productive_moa.description: Potential HA-antigen-loss escape; the graft-versus-leukemia-without-GVHD benefit depends on the mismatched mHAg staying hematopoietic-restricted

overall: The only donor TCR-T aimed at the antigen axis the run was built around - highest ceiling, thinnest evidence, and hostage to a HA-1/HA-2 mismatch that genotyping the sibling pair will settle.

intervention_label: FLAMSA-RIC sequential chemotherapy + reduced-intensity allo-HCT + prophylactic DLI
expected_benefit: The best-characterized way to actually deliver a transplant in refractory disease: sequential cytoreduction straight into a reduced-intensity allograft with prophylactic DLI from day +120. Schmid's prospective cohort reported 88% CR and 42% 2-year OS, with the refractory / adverse-cytogenetics subgroup doing as well as lower-risk patients, and 31 of 75 used HLA-identical sibling donors.
key_risks: GVHD, including prophylactic-DLI-associated GVHD, is the dominant risk and per-term toxicity is not tabulated in the source abstract
an older regimen whose conditioning intensity depends on the undocumented cardiac / organ-function fitness
overlaps with the HCT2 platform and Iomab-B conditioning rather than adding an independent modality
preference_alignment: Matches curative intent and the no-modality-veto set; it is a concrete sequencing route to the same transplant the plan depends on. Fitness data should set conditioning intensity.
guideline_status: Established conditioning regimen used for high-risk / refractory AML at transplant centers, more common in European practice; no distinct NCCN/ELN category of its own.
rationale_summary: Conservative ranked this as the concrete way to sequence a refractory marrow into HCT2 and was explicit that it overlaps with the transplant platform by design rather than competing with it. It is the chemotherapy-based alternative to Iomab-B conditioning (rank 3): the two aim at the same high-burden-disease problem, and the choice between them is a transplant-center decision informed by fitness. Its matched-sibling-donor subgroup mirrors her donor situation, and the prophylactic-DLI schedule dovetails with any post-transplant HLA-restricted TCR-T consolidation. No persona dissented; it simply sits behind the RCT-grade Iomab-B evidence on strength of design.
open_questions: Whether the treating transplant center runs FLAMSA-RIC sequencing
How it compares, for this patient, with targeted Iomab-B conditioning
How the prophylactic-DLI component is folded in alongside any TCR-T consolidation
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate - 88% CR and 42% 2-year OS in refractory / adverse-karyotype AML (Schmid 2005), matched-sibling subset included; delivers HCT2 in refractory disease.
toxicity_burden: High (GVHD and prophylactic-DLI-associated GVHD dominant; non-relapse mortality; conditioning organ toxicity)

counter_productive_moa.description: Prophylactic-DLI GVHD without proportional graft-versus-leukemia if disease burden is not reduced first

overall: The chemo-based conditioning alternative to Iomab-B for the same transplant job; a transplant-center choice, not an independent modality, with the prophylactic-DLI schedule dovetailing into consolidation.

intervention_label: Dual CD33/CD123 compound CAR-T (CD123-CD33 cCAR; CLL-1/CD33/CD123 CAR-T)
expected_benefit: The antigen-escape hedge the profile flags: her relapse already shows clonal evolution, so a compound CAR-T hitting both CD33 and CD123 covers both antigens she carries. The dual construct beat single-antigen targeting for survival across four AML xenograft models.
key_risks: No clinical efficacy data at all - the case is entirely xenograft-based, with no post-allo-HCT human experience
CRS plus on-target myeloablation of normal CD33- and CD123-positive progenitors, with no clinical toxicity table to plan against
recruiting sites are in mainland China; US insurers generally do not cover China-based trial care
preference_alignment: Trial-acceptable including travel and consistent with the curative goal and no-modality-veto set, but the earliest-phase evidence of any pick and an out-of-country access route.
guideline_status: Investigational, no approval anywhere; not in NCCN or ELN.
rationale_summary: The risktaker and advocate ranked this last on their own slates as an explicit longshot antigen-escape hedge, defensible given the documented 2019-to-2026 clonal evolution. Conservative dissented on safety: a dual CD33/CD123 CAR-T stacks CRS with on-target myeloablation of normal progenitors in a re-transplant candidate, and xenograft survival curves do not tell a clinician how to manage the patient. It is carried with caveats rather than as a clean recommendation because the evidence is entirely preclinical and the recruiting sites are in China, so the practical route is uncertain even before the post-allo-HCT eligibility and manufacturing questions. If a trial slot does not materialize, on-label gemtuzumab (rank 4) is the immediately available CD33 alternative.
open_questions: Whether either China-based sponsor will accept an overseas patient and US geography
Post-allo-HCT CAR-T eligibility, CRS management, and manufacturing feasibility
Quantitative CD33/CD123 antigen density to gate the construct choice
likelihood_of_effect: Speculative - dual-antigen CAR-T outperformed single-antigen across four AML xenografts (Petrov 2018); zero human efficacy data, no post-allo-HCT experience.
toxicity_burden: Unknown - no clinical data (expected CRS and on-target myeloablation of normal CD33/CD123 progenitors)

counter_productive_moa.description: On-target myeloablation of normal CD33/CD123 progenitors compounds marrow aplasia in a re-transplant candidate; CRS; no post-HCT data

overall: The dual-antigen escape hedge for a clonally evolving relapse, held back by xenograft-only evidence and China-only trial access; gemtuzumab is the available CD33 fallback.

intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (Decnupaz, IMGN632, CD123 ADC) as cytoreductive bridge
expected_benefit: A CD123 ADC with single-agent activity against her confirmed CD123-positive blasts: ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40) and composite CR 17% at the recommended phase 2 dose, without re-running the FLAG-IDA scaffold the disease already failed. Preclinically it kills AML at low picomolar potency and reaches the leukemic stem-cell compartment while sparing normal progenitors.
key_risks: Reversible veno-occlusive disease surfaced as a dose-limiting toxicity (2/68) and carries a boxed warning - the wrong hepatic risk to stack into a planned HCT2
one treatment-related death (1%) against a modest 21% ORR
benefit is density-dependent and quantitative CD123 flow is still pending
preference_alignment: An efficacy-leaning bridge that clears the no-veto, trial-acceptable filter, but the VOD signal cuts against it with a transplant ahead, and two personas preferred the on-label CD33 handle for the same job.
guideline_status: FDA-approved for BPDCN (Decnupaz, May 2026); off-label and off-guideline for AML, absent from NCCN AML v4.2026 and ELN 2022. Both AML-relevant trials are closed to new enrollment, so off-label is the more actionable path.
rationale_summary: The risktaker and advocate ranked pivekimab as a CD123-directed bridge that debulks without re-using a failed backbone. Concensusite dissented on guideline grounds - it is off-guideline for AML while on-label gemtuzumab covers the same debulk-before-HCT2 job at category 2A - and conservative flagged the peri-transplant VOD risk, preferring to sequence the on-label handle first until organ-function data land. With advocate framing it as preference-aligned and two personas dissenting, status is considered_with_caveats and the score lands at zero. The VOD signal is doubly relevant because the ADC is meant to bridge to the very transplant it could jeopardize. Tagraxofusp is the CD123 alternative but adds capillary-leak risk that argues even harder for fitness data first.
open_questions: Quantitative CD123 antigen density (antibodies-bound-per-cell), still pending
Whether the boxed VOD risk is acceptable given a planned HCT2, with the transplant team's input
Current off-label AML supply and prior-authorization route now that it is marketed for BPDCN
likelihood_of_effect: Low - single-agent ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40), composite CR 17% at RP2D (Daver 2024); density-directed selection still pending.
toxicity_burden: High (reversible veno-occlusive disease, febrile neutropenia 10%; one treatment-related death; peri-transplant hepatic risk)

counter_productive_moa.description: Reversible VOD could compromise the very HCT2 it is meant to bridge to; density-dependent activity unconfirmed on qualitative flow

overall: A CD123 ADC that debulks without a failed backbone, but its boxed VOD warning works against the transplant it bridges to and two personas prefer on-label gemtuzumab for the same job.

intervention_label: WT1 HLA-A*02:01 TCR-T (FH-WT1-E50 / Greenberg WT1-TCRc4); A*24:02 WT1-siTCR fallback
expected_benefit: Keeps the HLA-restricted axis alive if the HA-1/HA-2 pair does not mismatch but the patient is A*02:01-positive. The Chapuis WT1-TCRc4 work held 12 high-risk AML patients relapse-free post-transplant (100% RFS at median 44 months vs 54% in a concurrent cohort). If A*02:01 is negative, A*24:02 opens the WT1-siTCR lever, which is why both alleles should be typed in parallel.
key_risks: The evidence base is post-HCT relapse prophylaxis / MRD, not active-relapse salvage - a disease-state mismatch at 85% blasts
the 54% comparator is a concurrent non-randomized cohort, so the survival contrast is confounded (ROBINS-I Serious)
gated on A*02:01 (or A*24:02), still pending; the live product (FH-WT1-E50) is written for MRD-positive disease and not yet recruiting
preference_alignment: Same HLA-restricted, curative-intent, trial-acceptable profile the run was built around; kept explicitly so an A*02:01-positive but HA-non-mismatched result does not foreclose the immunotherapy axis the patient prioritized.
guideline_status: Investigational, no consensus category; trial enrollment is the guideline-preferred R/R route, and the A*24:02 siTCR fallback has no reachable US site.
rationale_summary: Conditional on HLA-A*02:01-positive (or A*24:02-positive for the siTCR alternative). Foreclosed if neither allele is present. Advocate ranked WT1 as the fallback lever that keeps the HLA-restricted axis open if HA-1/HA-2 does not mismatch, and was candid that it is weaker evidence with a disease-state mismatch. The critic dissented because the 100% RFS figure comes from a prophylaxis product given against relapse, not salvage of a florid marrow, on a confounded comparator; the risktaker separately noted the WT1 fallback bench is thinner than the ranking implies since it is relapse-prevention rather than active-disease evidence. Both dissents are about the evidence and the disease setting, which biomarker confirmation does not fix, so they persist in the positive branch. Best positioned as post-cytoreduction or post-HCT2 consolidation rather than for current-state disease.
open_questions: Whether the patient is A*02:01-positive, or A*24:02-positive for the siTCR fallback (both pending, typed in parallel)
When the live FH-WT1-E50 product (NCT07645469) opens and whether a post-cytoreduction path onto it is realistic
Whether any reachable A*24:02 WT1-siTCR site exists if A*02:01 is negative
scenario_label: If HLA-A*02:01-positive (or A*24:02-positive for the WT1-siTCR alternative)
likelihood_of_effect: Setting-mismatched, positive branch - 100% RFS at 44 months as post-HCT prophylaxis (Chapuis 2019, n=12, confounded comparator); unproven for florid relapse.
toxicity_burden: Low (engineered into EBV-specific cells to minimize GVHD; no per-term AE breakdown; on-target hematopoietic risk theoretical)

counter_productive_moa.description: Validated as relapse prophylaxis, not salvage; unproven against florid marrow disease; WT1 is a shared self-antigen

overall: The second HLA-restricted lever that keeps the immunotherapy axis open if HA-1/HA-2 does not mismatch, but its evidence is prophylaxis in MRD, not salvage of an 85%-blast marrow.

expected_benefit: A drug that physically refolds the exact mutant p53 back toward wild-type shape. In Y220C AML models it reactivates p53 and, paired with venetoclax or MDM2/XPO1 inhibition, restores real apoptotic killing; the solid-tumor PYNNACLE data show ORR 20% (30% in KRAS-wild-type). If TP53 is confirmed Y220C, NCT06616636 (rezatapopt + azacitidine) is the myeloid slot at MD Anderson.
key_risks: Zero myeloid clinical data - every response so far is in solid tumors, and the myeloid trial NCT06616636 has posted nothing
single-agent apoptosis is weak preclinically; it needs a venetoclax or MDM2/XPO1 partner, and she is already refractory to a venetoclax-containing regimen
grade >=3 anaemia 16%; predominant low-grade nausea and vomiting
preference_alignment: Efficacy-leaning and oral, trial-acceptable, but it sits off the HLA-restricted axis that is the stated reason for the run; advocate deliberately kept it off the preference-carrying slate. Worth resolving in parallel, not foregrounding.
guideline_status: Investigational; no AML guideline lists a p53 reactivator, and it appears in neither NCCN AML v4.2026 nor ELN 2022.
rationale_summary: Conditional on TP53 confirmed aberrant AND the specific variant confirmed as Y220C - a genuine double contingency off a 2019-mutant-versus-2026-negative discrepancy read on a 2%-LOD, CNV-blind panel. Even in the positive branch, the dissents persist because they are about the evidence base, not the biomarker: the critic marks it down for solid-tumor-only data and a venetoclax dependency she is already refractory to, and concensusite marks it off-consensus since no AML guideline carries a p53 reactivator and the myeloid trial has no results. Only the risktaker ranked it, as a mechanistic longshot. A non-Y220C aberration, or a true reversion to wild-type, forecloses it entirely; eprenetapopt is the low-yield pan-reactivator alternative and is functionally unavailable in myeloid disease.
open_questions: Whether the retrieved 2019 variant plus relapse NGS confirm a TP53 aberration, and specifically Y220C
Whether a venetoclax or MDM2/XPO1 partner can be given in a venetoclax-refractory patient
Whether the single-site myeloid trial (NCT06616636) can enroll her once the variant is confirmed
scenario_label: If TP53 is confirmed aberrant AND the variant is confirmed Y220C
likelihood_of_effect: Cross-tumor only, positive branch - solid-tumor ORR 20% (30% KRAS-WT, PYNNACLE); no myeloid clinical data; preclinically needs a venetoclax partner.
toxicity_burden: Low (grade >=3 anaemia 16%; predominant low-grade nausea 58% and vomiting 44%, less frequent with food)

counter_productive_moa.description: Reactivated p53 barely triggers apoptosis alone - it needs a venetoclax / MDM2 partner the patient is already refractory to

overall: A mechanistically elegant Y220C longshot off the stated axis, double-gated on confirming TP53 then Y220C, with no myeloid data and a venetoclax dependency she has already failed.
